ready_when: The current upstream Hermes Kanban source and tests are synced locally and read from source/test files only, not live user config.
The slice can use temp GORMES_HOME paths and fake worker names; no gateway, dashboard, subprocess workers, or live profile config is required.
SQLite is already an approved Gormes dependency through the existing ncruces/go-sqlite3 driver.
not_ready_when: The slice reads ~/.hermes, HERMES_HOME, profile configs, or other agents' memory outside explicit migrate commands.
The slice implies dispatcher, worker tools, slash/gateway routing, dashboard, multi-board management, notifications, or run logs are complete.
Task claiming is implemented as a read-then-write race instead of a single SQL update that only one process can win.

item.name: Hermes Kanban dispatcher and worker spawn loop
item.contract: Gormes ports the Hermes Kanban dispatcher core as a native gateway-managed loop with a fakeable worker-spawner seam: each tick reclaims stale claims, selects ready assigned tasks, claims through the store, records spawn attempts and spawn failures, passes GORMES_* worker context, respects max-spawn caps across successful and failed attempts, and blocks tasks behind a circuit breaker after repeated failures. Real OS process spawning, PID/crash detection, max-runtime termination, worker log rotation, and production config wiring remain a separate row.
item.degraded_mode: Missing profile binaries, spawn failures, exceeded runtime caps, stale worker heartbeats, and locked databases report dispatcher_unavailable, worker_spawn_failed, worker_timed_out, or task_circuit_open evidence without infinite retry loops.
ready_when: Hermes Kanban durable board core is complete.
Gormes has a profile/process spawn seam that can be faked in tests without launching live agent sessions.
Run records, heartbeats, and log paths are modeled in the Kanban store before gateway wiring.
not_ready_when: The slice shells out to Hermes Python, reads live Hermes profile config, or starts real workers in unit tests.
A crashed worker leaves a task permanently running with no TTL reclaim evidence.
Permanent failures retry forever instead of opening a circuit and requiring operator input.
unblocks: Hermes Kanban worker tools and prompt gating
acceptance: Dispatcher fixtures prove dry-run output, ready-task selection, max-spawn caps, and no-op behavior when no ready tasks exist.
Stale-claim fixtures prove expired running tasks return to ready with reclaim evidence.
Spawn fixtures prove worker env includes the Gormes task id, board path, assignee/profile, and workspace details without leaking other agents' config.
Failure fixtures prove retry counts, failed-spawn recovery, and circuit breaker block after the configured failure limit.
Gateway lifecycle fixtures prove the dispatcher is owned by the gateway loop and can be nudged without starting duplicate daemons.
item.note: Complete: TDD landed the fakeable dispatcher core and gateway-owned lifecycle seam. RunOnce reclaims expired running claims, lists ready tasks in priority/created order, respects MaxSpawn across successful and failed claimed attempts, skips unassigned tasks, claims through the existing atomic store path, resolves Gormes-owned workspaces, passes only GORMES_* worker context to the injected spawner, records spawned attempts, records failed spawn attempts, and auto-blocks with circuit-breaker evidence at FailureLimit. The gateway Manager owns an injectable Kanban dispatcher loop with deterministic tick/nudge channels, runtime status JSON evidence, degraded last_error handling that does not crash the gateway, exact trigger timestamps, clean shutdown, restart-after-stop ownership release, and closed test-channel shutdown protection. item.name: Hermes Kanban production worker process binding
item.contract: Gormes binds the fakeable Kanban dispatcher spawner to a production worker launcher that resolves Gormes profiles, resolves the default worker executable with PATH-first `gormes` lookup and current-executable fallback for stripped cron/systemd PATHs, builds the native gormes worker argv/env with Kanban context pins and the kanban-worker skill, redirects stdout/stderr to per-task logs with bounded rotation, records worker PID/run metadata, detects crashed worker PIDs, enforces per-task max-runtime caps through injected process controls, and reports worker_spawn_failed, worker_crashed, worker_timed_out, or task_circuit_open evidence without reading live Hermes config.
item.degraded_mode: Explicitly configured missing gormes binaries, invalid profile names, unwritable workspaces/log paths, stale PIDs, process-kill failures, and max-runtime expiry return typed evidence and release or block the task according to the dispatcher failure policy; default worker spawns fall back to the current executable when PATH lacks `gormes` and never spawn Hermes Python.

The builder can inject fake process start, PID liveness, signal/kill, log filesystem, and clock seams; no unit test starts or kills a real worker process.

item.name: Hermes Kanban worker tools and prompt gating
item.contract: Gormes exposes Hermes-compatible worker tools for Kanban tasks: kanban_show, kanban_complete, kanban_block, kanban_heartbeat, kanban_comment, kanban_create, and kanban_link are only visible inside a Kanban worker task or explicit profile toolset, enforce task ownership for destructive operations, and carry structured parent summaries/metadata to children.
item.degraded_mode: Outside a Kanban worker context the tools are hidden or return kanban_context_missing; attempts to complete, block, or heartbeat a foreign task return kanban_task_ownership_denied without mutating the board. Kanban comment cross-task handoff and author hardening are owned by the completed follow-up child row.

Completion summaries or metadata are stored as opaque logs only and cannot flow to child context.
acceptance: Tool visibility fixtures prove Kanban tools are hidden without worker context and visible with HERMES/GORMES-style task context or enabled profile toolset.

item.name: Kanban worker heartbeat, reclaim, and zombie detection
item.contract: Kanban workers emit a heartbeat at a configurable interval; the dispatcher reclaims tasks whose worker heartbeat is stale beyond the threshold, marks the worker as zombie, and re-enqueues the task with retry budget honored. Auto-block on incomplete worker exit, darwin zombie detection, and a unified failure counter across spawn/timeout/crash outcomes are part of the same contract. Mirrors Hermes v0.13.0 PRs #21183, #21214, #20188, #20410.
item.degraded_mode: Without heartbeat reclaim, a hung worker holds its task forever and the dispatcher cannot reassign; status reports show worker=stale and task=held with last-seen timestamp instead of pretending the work is in progress.
ready_when: 5.M `Hermes Kanban dispatcher and worker spawn loop` is complete and exposes a worker-state seam reachable from tests.
2.E.3 `Durable worker supervisor status seam` heartbeat states (no-worker, healthy, stale, supervisor-unavailable) are present and reusable.
Fake clock and fake worker controllers exist in tests so heartbeat timing can be exercised without real subprocesses.
not_ready_when: The slice spawns real worker subprocesses to test heartbeat timing.
Reclaim path silently drops a task's retry budget when promoting it back to the queue.
Zombie detection collapses with healthy-but-slow workers because the threshold is not configurable.
darwin-specific detection is hidden behind unconditional Linux-only assumptions.

acceptance: TestKanbanWorker_HeartbeatStaleReclaim proves a worker whose heartbeat exceeds threshold is marked zombie and its task is re-enqueued with the retry budget decremented exactly once.
TestKanbanWorker_HeartbeatHealthyDoesNotReclaim proves an active worker is never reclaimed.
TestKanbanWorker_FailureCounterUnified proves spawn-failure, timeout, and crash each increment the same counter and reflect in dispatcher status.
TestKanbanWorker_DarwinZombieDetected proves darwin-specific PID-state detection runs on darwin and returns 'unknown' on other GOOS without panicking.

item.name: Hermes Kanban specify triage parity
